transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Recording ID: ff-20250312-vertopt-001
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Chu (Redwood SE), Lena Gomez (Redwood Product), Dr. Aaron Blake (Vertex CTO), Sofia Marin (Vertex ML Eng), Ravi Singh (Vertex Infra)
Links shared: deck: https://rwd.co/decks/optimize-quant-2025, benchmark sheet: https://rwd.co/sheets/vert-quant-bench-03-12

[00:00] Maya Patel (AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time, uh we've got about 45 minutes today, we want to focus on Optimize's quantization profiles and the practical quality vs latency tradeoffs for your pilot, especially given the constraints you mentioned in the discovery call.
[01:02] Dr. Aaron Blake: great, thanks Maya. quick note, timeline is still Q2 pilot start, security approvals in flight. we care about sub-200ms 95th latency for short clinical completions, and costs matter since this will be user-facing.
[02:15] Evan Chu (SE): mm-hmm, and just to set expectations — int8 historically gives the biggest cost/throughput wins across our tests, fp8 is interesting, it's newer, can sit between int8 and fp16 in terms of memory and throughput but with different quantization noise patterns. i'll demo the console and then show live traces.
[03:40] Sofia Marin: one thing i wanted to flag, our prompts average 600 tokens per request including history, and we have prefix caching for templates. will that change the benefits from int8?
[04:10] Evan: good question — caching helps a lot. int8 primarily reduces model memory footprint which lets you push more concurrent requests through batching and increases tokens/sec; but if your workload is dominated by long context KV cache hits, the per-token compute still matters. OPTimize will recommend different profiles depending on your token distribution.
[06:00] Lena Gomez (Product): i'm sharing my screen — this is the Optimize console, the profiling tab. you can see the suggested quantization profile matrix on the left. for Vertex's sample trace we uploaded, Optimize suggests INT8/awq for 80% of requests, and FP8 for specific high-accuracy prompts.
[07:20] [screen share: console – show latency vs quality chart]
[07:35] Dr. Aaron Blake: awq? excuse me — what does awq stand for?
[07:40] Evan: AWQ is a per-tensor asymmetric quantization variant that preserves some of the outlier weights better than straight linear int8 — it's often why int8 with AWQ has smaller quality regressions. transcript note: awq sometimes transcribed as a-w-q or 'a w q'.
[09:00] Maya: we often present three buckets — conservative (fp16/fp32), balanced (fp8 fallback + int8 for bulk), and aggressive (int8-first, fp8 for edges). for Vertex, given you want low 95th latency, we recommended balanced as a starting point.
[11:30] Ravi Singh: on infra, what changes do we need on the runtime? we're using our VPC dedicated nodes with NVIDIA A10s right now.
[12:10] Evan: good, A10s are supported. INT8 and FP8 kernels rely on the same runtime but we pick different fused kernels/implementations. there's no infra-level change beyond making sure your driver stack and cuBLAS/cuDNN versions are aligned; we'll provide a checklist in the SOC2 doc. some fp8 paths are experimental and benefit more from A100 or H100 in our benchmarks.
[13:55] Sofia: do you have numbers — like 95th latency improvements or token/sec uplift from int8 vs fp16?
[14:20] Evan: yes, for a 6B-ish model on A10s with our engine: int8 (AWQ) shows ~1.8-2.2x tokens/sec improvement vs fp16 and 25-40% reduction in 95th latency under our batch mix. fp8 in our tests gave ~1.4-1.7x and sometimes had slightly better quality on certain tasks depending on calibration. those ranges are workload dependent.
[16:05] Dr. Aaron: when you say calibration, what do you need from us?
[16:25] Evan: a representative prompt set is ideal — 5-10k examples for calibration across the prompt types you expect. Optimize can run automatic calibration and produce per-prompt quality delta metrics. we compare perplexity, and also run your business evals if you provide them.
[18:40] [19:00] Maya: quick aside — people sometimes conflate FP8 as universally better; it's not always. FP8 can be good for certain transformer ops and reduces memory more than fp16 but less than int8; however calibration and per-layer sensitivity matter.
[20:15] Speaker 1 (unclear): is there a fallback in runtime if quality drops?
[20:30] Evan: yes — rollout policies. you can set per-route policies to try int8 and if quality delta on a sampled fraction exceeds threshold, automatically fallback to fp16 or fp8. we demo the canary flow in the console.
[22:00] [console demo — rollout flows and trace playback]
[24:10] Sofia: showing the benchmark sheet now — the sample CSV we uploaded had 8k prompts; Optimize's recommendation column flags which prompts are sensitive to int8. i see about 6% of prompts have >2% QA metric drop under int8.
[25:05] Evan: yep, and for those prompts Optimize suggests pinning them to fp8 or fp16, or enabling prefix caching so less compute runs. you can also whitelist prompt templates to force higher precision.
[26:30] Dr. Aaron: for the user-facing workflows, we can't have visible regressions on diagnostic phrasing; how do you measure "visible"?
[26:50] Lena: we use a mix — automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity depending on task) and human-in-the-loop checks for critical prompts. Optimize supports uploading human evals and will correlate failures to quantization changes.
[28:10] Maya: also worth noting — cost math. for your expected QPS, moving to int8-first balanced profile is ~30-45% lower infra cost vs fp16 in our sample runs assuming the same SLOs, because you can fit more replicas per GPU and reduce evictions.
[30:00] Ravi: about monitoring — will console show token-level cost impact and breakdowns?
[30:20] Evan: yes, the Cost Analyst view shows token-level, model-level, and route-level breakdowns. here i pull up the cost curve for the same workload with int8 vs fp8 vs fp16. [screen flicker] you can see the crossover points where latency SLOs start to fail.
[32:00] Dr. Aaron: are there any known model classes where int8 just doesn't work? like retrieval-augmented generation with long contexts?
[32:25] Evan: retrieval plus very long contexts amplifies kv cache memory pressure. int8 helps with model weights but not the kv cache — so net benefit can be smaller. for extremely long contexts we sometimes recommend mixed strategies: fp16 for long-history routes, int8 for short interactive completions.
[34:15] Sofia: can Optimize automate A/B style rollouts to measure quality delta? we want a statistically significant test without exposing all users.
[34:35] Maya: yes — you can configure traffic splits and sample ratios; Optimize will compute delta metrics and surface confidence intervals. it's not a full MLOps stats engine but it covers the common cases.
[36:20] [minor crosstalk, someone muted/unmuted]
[37:00] Evan: for implementation: we'll provide a pilot script to run 1) a calibration job, 2) a small canary rollout, and 3) a full performance run. we'll upload a compass of recommended kernel flags; note fp8 kernels still get tuned per-arch in our runtime.
[38:40] Dr. Aaron: any constraints around data residency or PII during calibration? we need assurance the calibration jobs don't leak patient text to Redwood.
[38:55] Lena: good question — for hosted we obfuscate and we offer Private (VPC or on-prem) where the calibration runs inside your environment and only the aggregate metrics are visible to Redwood. we'll share the SOC2 and private deployment checklist.
[40:10] Maya: recap and next steps — i'll attach the benchmark sheet and deck, Evan will run the int8 pilot, Sofia will provide the 10k prompts, and Lena will share SOC2/KMS checklists.
[41:05] Ravi: timeline looks ok. also please include a cost estimate for a dedicated pool that meets our expected QPS with balanced profile.
[42:30] Maya: noted — we'll include a couple of sizing options.
[43:15] Dr. Aaron: thanks all, this was helpful. one last thing — you mentioned fp8 being 'experimental' — is it production supported?
[43:40] Evan: supported with caveats. we consider fp8 supported in Redwood Dedicated and Private with guarded fallbacks; in Hosted it's available but we recommend pilot validation. we'll add that language to the writeup.
[45:00] Maya: ok wrapping up — i'll follow up with the files and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff the week of 3/24. thanks everyone.
[46:10] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of acronyms (AWQ -> a w q), some speaker attribution uncertain around 36-37m.
